Copied Arbitrum gateway mint inventory on PulseChain
Research date: 29 September 2026. This is a bounded, read-only census of existing router registrations,
destination gateway implementations and token permissions. It interprets recorded transactions; it does
not construct transactions or assume that a copied L1 contract proves the existence of a corresponding
running L2.
Findings
There is more than one destination issuance model. ARB has a confirmed direct bridgeMint
integration and an observed post-fork mint. GRT has a different, authorized, allowance-
limited mint integration and an observed post-fork mint. LPT has a source-confirmed external-
minter branch for escrow shortfalls, but this batch does not verify the current external minter's
implementation. HGOLD has a registered gateway whose source calls bridgeMint, but its token source and
current token-level permission remain unverified. WETH wraps native currency received by its gateway;
this is another form of issuance with different backing.
These findings rule out an ARB-only account of the copied infrastructure. They do not establish generic
issuance of existing stablecoins or Aave receipt tokens. In particular, the queried OUSD, eUSD, mUSD,
FRAX and three Aave v3 receipt-token addresses select the standard gateway, whose inbound operation
transfers existing L1 escrow. Routing to that gateway does not grant it the token's issuer role.
Pin, method and census boundary
All endpoint storage and view reads use block 27,659,393 (0x1a60c81), hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275. The inherited snapshot boundary is block 
17,232,999. Event searches use the public PulseChain RPC's available history from block zero through
the endpoint, including inherited Ethereum events, and distinguish post-fork events from that inherited
history. Transaction observations additionally retain their own block hashes. No public state was
changed.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 44

Router 0x72ce9c846789fdb6fc1f34ac4ad25dd9ef7031ef returned 167 GatewaySet events covering 129
distinct L1 token addresses. The last event per token was reconciled against the router's endpoint 
getGateway result. This produces 98 standard-gateway routes (including five default fallbacks), 20 custom-
gateway routes, four disabled routes, and seven single-token specialized routes. There are nine
nonzero destination gateway addresses in this census. Seven named assets were also queried,
producing 136 endpoint token reads in total.
This is complete for the returned router event set, not for every ERC20 on PulseChain. The standard
gateway's default makes unregistered addresses resolve to a gateway too. Such resolution does not
prove a historical deposit, usable counterpart token, available escrow, or successful withdrawal. Direct
gateway registrations that are never selected by this router, arbitrary future contracts, other routers and
unrelated issuer mechanisms are outside this census. Full registration logs were additionally obtained for
the ARB and HGOLD reverse-like gateways; each returned one registered token pair.
Implementation slots were read at the pinned endpoint rather than assuming the May 2023
implementation still applied. Verified explorer source was retrieved for each identified implementation or
direct gateway. A zero EIP-1967 slot alone is not treated as proof that an arbitrary contract has no other
indirection; source availability and observed call paths determine the narrower conclusions.

Primary source records are the explorer's verified contracts for the standard gateway implementation, 
custom gateway implementation, GRT implementation, WETH implementation, DAI gateway, LPT
gateway, wstETH implementation, ARB implementation and HGOLD gateway. The saved API responses
preserve the actual source retrieved, including inherited base contracts; the explorer links alone are not
substitutes for the pinned reads.
ARB: direct bridgeMint, historically executed
L1 ARB is 0xb50721bcf8d664c30412cfbc6cf7a15145234ad1. The reverse gateway's single T okenSet event pairs it
with L2 address 0x912ce59144191c1204e64559fe8253a0e49e6548 at block 16,840,312, transaction 0x5cc80a28….
Router selection followed at block 16,840,532, transaction 0x5c3e3b15…. Both are inherited
registrations, not post-fork changes.
The token's verified implementation authorizes its configured arbOneGateway to call bridgeMint and 
bridgeBurn; the prior pinned audit verified that getter points to this reverse gateway. The successful post-
fork mint in transaction 0xeebae5bc…, block 21,469,490, is established by receipt, trace and supply
change in the bridge observations (Appendix 5).
This proves exact-token destination issuance. The same study records malformed accepted source
metadata and does not claim independently verified L2 escrow. Successful destination execution and
economic source backing are separate facts.
GRT: verified issuance bounded by an accumulating allowance
L1 GRT is 0xc944e90c64b2c07662a292be6244bdf05cda44a7. Its specialized router registration is inherited block
16,149,151, transaction 0x844a8a3a…. The gateway verifies the token identity and accepted
counterpart. If an incoming amount exceeds escrow, _mintFromL2 checks its accumulated allowance,
increments totalMintedFromL2, calls GraphToken.mint(escrow, shortfall), and then transfers the complete
incoming amount from escrow to its recipient. This is a GRT-specific issuance mechanism, not the ARB 
bridgeMint token interface.
At the endpoint, GraphToken.isMinter(gateway) returns true and the gateway's paused() returns false. Its
recorded state is:
Quantity GRT units
T otal minted through this allowance 62,875,936.675361278837595998
Cumulative allowance at block 27,659,393 64,230,816.8555
Difference between allowance and recorded minted
amount
1,354,880.180138721162404002
Allowance accrual per block under current settings 6.0365
The allowance difference is an accounting ceiling at the pinned block, not a promise of executable future
transfers or a dollar value. Escrow transfers, authentication and other token checks still apply. Future
configuration is not assumed fixed.

Exactly one T okensMintedFromL2 event was returned in the searched history: transaction 0xf7ed5701…,
block 27,434,949, hash 0xbc7a6608cbb7515daaa1464f02cf94fc162b9f89c8c7a0a2859d140c575dd4bb, 1 September
2026, 13:42:05 UTC. The receipt succeeds. Its trace follows the outbox, bridge, GRT gateway and
currently identified gateway implementation, then calls GraphT oken.mint and GraphT oken.transferFrom.
The token emits a zero-address mint to escrow 0x36aff7001294dae4c2ed4fdefc478a00de77f090 for 
62,875,936.675361278837595998 GRT, matching the gateway event. The escrow then transfers the
withdrawal amount to 0xa0b347117a878da9942fa5c31b87c773a2969913.
T otal supply between the preceding block and this block rises by precisely the same mint amount. The
external transaction sender is 0xfbba783afda7b41ebb7473a914f0b6eb9f9139f3. No common human ownership is
inferred from these addresses. This batch proves destination issuance; it does not independently
authenticate an L2 lock, source burn or source state history.
LPT and HGOLD: explicit limits on confirmation
LPT, 0x58b6a8a3302369daec383334672404ee733ab239, selects its dedicated gateway through inherited block
14,207,632, transaction 0x994651c7…. The gateway's verified finalizeInboundTransfer transfers
available LPT from l1LPTEscrow, then calls minter.bridgeMint for any shortfall. Endpoint getters identify
escrow 0x6a23f4940bd5ba117da261f98aae51a8bffa210a and minter 0x8dddb96cf36ac8860f1de5c7c4698fd499fab405. The
token's owner getter returns that same minter. Verified LivepeerT oken source restricts its ordinary mint
method to its owner and additionally checks that minting is not finished.
However, the configured minter source was unavailable in this batch. Its getter identifies controller 
0xf96d54e490317c557a967abfa5d6e33006be69b3, but that alone does not prove which gateway callers it accepts.
This study therefore classifies LPT as an identified issuance branch with an unresolved current external-
minter permission check, not a newly demonstrated successful bridge mint.
HGOLD (Hashgold) is 0x445164d9e038e1dae0989e4b6ac745b78d26f181. The gateway's sole T okenSet event maps
the same numeric address on both sides; router registration occurs in the same inherited block
16,971,420, transaction 0x24371101…. The verified gateway overrides inbound escrow handling to
invoke the token's bridgeMint and outbound handling to invoke bridgeBurn.
The token's endpoint name and symbol getters identify Hashgold/HGOLD, but the explorer returned no
verified token source. Its EIP-1967 slot was zero, and speculative gateway getters reverted; neither
result establishes issuer permissions. The zero-address Transfer search returned 85 inherited mint logs
and no post-fork mint logs through the endpoint. Inspection of the last such inherited transaction shows
a direct token call, not a bridge call. Those mint logs therefore do not prove a successful HGOLD
bridgeMint integration. It remains a registered source-supported gateway path with unverified token-
level behavior.

These are exact-address routing observations, not a census of all stablecoins, all Aave deployments, all
Balancer wrappers, or every similarly named token. This batch does not inspect governance actions in
Origin, Reserve or Morpho. Nor does it assess pool liquidity or establish that routing to a standard
gateway makes a rebasing receipt safe to bridge. Aave Portal's pool-authorized issuance is a separate
accounting mechanism; it is not conferred by router registration.
What token type does and does not establish
An ordinary transferable ERC20, including an ERC20 called a PRC20 on PulseChain, can be a custody
asset for an appropriately implemented reverse bridge. ERC4626 vault shares also expose ERC20
balances and can represent source collateral that remains invested. The destination representation has
the redemption rights its actual implementation grants. Rebasing receipts require compatible
accounting; locking a rebasing balance does not automatically synchronize destination shares. ERC721
and ERC1155 require different custody and message semantics and are not made compatible with these
ERC20 gateways by registration alone.
Three checks must remain distinct: routing/registration, authenticated bridge execution, and the
exact destination token's issuance permission. A fourth is the economic question of independently
evidenced source backing. The ARB and GRT destination examples answer the first three for particular
recorded transactions. They do not replace the fourth or transfer permissions to unrelated stablecoins.
The historical bridge model study (Appendix 13) explains native-L2 custody and L1 representation
accounting in more detail.
Reproduction records
Raw observations are preserved under ignored artifacts/parb-bridge-mint-inventory-20260929/. The batch
includes router event logs, the 129-token event inventory, 136 endpoint routing reads, reverse-gateway
registrations, nine endpoint implementation reads and verified source responses, token permission
reads, GRT mint logs/receipt/trace/block/supply comparison, and HGOLD mint-log and sampled-
transaction observations. The manifest records the endpoint and file hashes. Earlier ARB transaction and
token evidence remains in the separate historical bridge batches cited by the companion study.
This study's strongest new result is an actual GRT-specific, authorized and allowance-limited
destination issuance, alongside ARB's reverse-token issuance. No evidence collected here makes the
named stablecoin or Aave-token routes operate as those specialized minting integrations.
Follow-up transaction audit
The GRT reconciliation (Appendix 12) establishes that the September withdrawal combined 1 existing
GRT with the recorded mint, and that its allowance parameters and minter permission were inherited. Its
historical source design burns withdrawn GRT on L2. The escrow receipt census (Appendix 11) screens
102 additional withdrawal events across four gateway addresses and identifies a retired LPT gateway,
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 48

expanding historical gateway-address coverage to ten. The specialized history (Appendix 20) classifies
the recorded LPT withdrawal as an escrow release, with no minter call and no block-to-block supply
increase. Source capability and executed issuance remain separate findings.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 49

These are exact-address routing observations, not a census of all stablecoins, all Aave deployments, all
Balancer wrappers, or every similarly named token. This batch does not inspect governance actions in
Origin, Reserve or Morpho. Nor does it assess pool liquidity or establish that routing to a standard
gateway makes a rebasing receipt safe to bridge. Aave Portal's pool-authorized issuance is a separate
accounting mechanism; it is not conferred by router registration.
What token type does and does not establish
An ordinary transferable ERC20, including an ERC20 called a PRC20 on PulseChain, can be a custody
asset for an appropriately implemented reverse bridge. ERC4626 vault shares also expose ERC20
balances and can represent source collateral that remains invested. The destination representation has
the redemption rights its actual implementation grants. Rebasing receipts require compatible
accounting; locking a rebasing balance does not automatically synchronize destination shares. ERC721
and ERC1155 require different custody and message semantics and are not made compatible with these
ERC20 gateways by registration alone.
Three checks must remain distinct: routing/registration, authenticated bridge execution, and the
exact destination token's issuance permission. A fourth is the economic question of independently
evidenced source backing. The ARB and GRT destination examples answer the first three for particular
recorded transactions. They do not replace the fourth or transfer permissions to unrelated stablecoins.
The historical bridge model study (Appendix 13) explains native-L2 custody and L1 representation
accounting in more detail.
Reproduction records
Raw observations are preserved under ignored artifacts/parb-bridge-mint-inventory-20260929/. The batch
includes router event logs, the 129-token event inventory, 136 endpoint routing reads, reverse-gateway
registrations, nine endpoint implementation reads and verified source responses, token permission
reads, GRT mint logs/receipt/trace/block/supply comparison, and HGOLD mint-log and sampled-
transaction observations. The manifest records the endpoint and file hashes. Earlier ARB transaction and
token evidence remains in the separate historical bridge batches cited by the companion study.
This study's strongest new result is an actual GRT-specific, authorized and allowance-limited
destination issuance, alongside ARB's reverse-token issuance. No evidence collected here makes the
named stablecoin or Aave-token routes operate as those specialized minting integrations.
